ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Constitution of Colombia (1991), Articles 58 and 333; Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada regime); Colombian Commercial Code (Decree 410 of 1971), Book II; Law 526 of 1999 (creation of UIAF); Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT and PEP framework); Law 1778 of 2016 (transparency and anti-bribery); UIAF Resolution 202 of 2018 (identification of final beneficiaries); Decree 830 of 2021 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales managed by DIAN); Decree 2195 of 2021 (anti-corruption regulations); Superintendencia de Sociedades Circular Básica Jurídica No. 100-000003 of 2020 and amendments; INVIMA Decree 4725 of 2005 and Resolution 4818 of 2018 (medical devices registration and GMP)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and legal representatives against (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, (ii) OFAC SDN list, (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions register, (iv) INTERPOL notices, and (v) Colombian UIAF 'Listas Vinculantes'; domestic PEP determination per Law 1121 of 2006 Article 2 and UIAF Resolution 202 of 2018; enhanced due diligence required for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and any unusual transaction patterns; suspicious transaction reports filed through UIAF SIROS (Sistema de Reportes Operativos) within statutory deadlines; negative screening results must be documented for a minimum of ten years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) at www.rues.org.co operated jointly by Confecámaras and the competent local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá for a Bogota domicile)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Spanish or in a Latin-script alphabet; foreign-language names and acronyms are acceptable provided they are transliterated into Latin characters and are pronounceable in Spanish; names must not be misleading as to the corporate form, purpose, or permitted activities; the mandatory corporate determinant 'S.A.S.' must appear in the registered name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a reserved name, the applicant may (i) immediately submit a new name request through RUES without penalty; (ii) file an administrative reconsideration appeal ('recurso de reposición') with the competent Cámara de Comercio within ten business days of the rejection notice, arguing that no identical or confusingly similar name exists on the registry; (iii) file a subsidiary appeal ('recurso de apelación') to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within the same ten-business-day window; (iv) if the rejection is based on a third-party trademark or trade name, the applicant may request a release of the name by filing a notarized authorization or resolving the conflict amicably through the Cámara de Comercio mediation service; the reservation cannot be extended beyond 30 calendar days, but a wholly new application may be filed at no additional substantive cost beyond the re-application fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited virtual office acceptance for legal domicile and service of process purposes only; the registered address must be a real physical location where notices can be served during business hours. For an ISIC 3250 electronic patient monitor assembly plant, INVIMA requires a physical manufacturing and calibration facility compliant with Good Manufacturing Practices under Decree 4725 of 2005; a virtual office cannot satisfy the GMP inspection, telemetry calibration, traceability, or sterile/controlled environment requirements. The SAS may maintain a virtual commercial correspondence office separate from the mandatory operational plant address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Mandatory pre-incorporation milestone: INVIMA pre-market GMP inspection is essentially certain (near 100%) before approval of the manufacturer's registration for a Class 2B multi-parameter bedside telemetry monitor under Colombian Resolution 4818 of 2018; post-market surveillance inspections are highly probable (estimated 60-70% annual likelihood for this medical device class); unannounced Chamber of Commerce verification visits to the registered office occur at a low but non-negligible rate (estimated 5-10%); therefore a fully physical, lease-backed premises is required from first day of operations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Articles 1-10, 30 for S.A.S. formation); Código de Comercio (Libro II, Título VI, Articles 110-120) for commercial registration; Decreto 1074 de 2015 (Chapter on commercial registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) - Registro Mercantil, coordinated with DIAN for tax registration (RUT).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Private Incorporation Deed) filed as 'Inscripción de la Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada en el Registro Único Empresarial y Social (R.U.E.S.)'. Public deed (Escritura Pública) required if real property is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital is freely determined in by-laws and may be contributed in cash, in-kind, or services. No escrow account is required. Foreign-currency contributions must be registered with Banco de la República if external capital is introduced.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders comprising the constitutive assembly of the S.A.S. hereby approve the subscription and issuance of share capital as set forth in the certificate of incorporation, fully subscribed by the founding shareholders. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company shall be established at [insert address] in Bogotá D.C., Colombia, and that notice of any change shall be filed with the Cámara de Comercio. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as sole Administrator/General Manager and [Name], if applicable, as Legal Representative, with powers to execute ordinary and extraordinary corporate acts, open bank accounts, and sign contracts. RESOLVED, that the appointed officials accept their positions and are reminded of their fiduciary duties under Law 1258 of 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or local Chamber of Commerce) — Certification of Homonymy/Name Availability via virtual portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name and up to three alternative names through the Chamber's 'Agenda Virtual' or online registration search. The Chamber will issue a 'Certificado de Homonímia' confirming no identical registered trade name exists. For a S.A.S., the name must end with 'S.A.S.' and this suffix is checked.
required_dossiers: Completed name search form
National ID or passport of each subscribing shareholder
Business description (ISIC 3250)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, immediately file a new request with alternative names or wait 30 days for the prior certificate to expire.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Private Incorporation Document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and, where applicable, a Colombian Notary Public (Notaría)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the 'Documento Privado de Constitución' of the S.A.S., expressing the will to form the company, share subscription amount, duration, registered office address, and administrative structure. If real property is contributed, elevate the document to 'Escritura Pública' before a notary. Sign in the presence of a notary or witnesses as required.
required_dossiers: Certificate of availability name
Copy of shareholders' identification
Draft by-laws containing capital, shares, and voting rules
RUT for each shareholder (if previously registered)
Proof of legal domicile (lease or title deed if real property contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify formal errors in the draft and resubmit for signature; notarization defects are curable by affidavit of the subscribing shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration with Cámara de Comercio (Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio — 'Registro Único Empresarial' (RUE) / 'Registro Mercantil'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed incorporation document and required forms through the Chamber's 'SIL' online platform or at the regional 'Prestación de Servicios' window. Pay the applicable registration and matrícula mercantil fees. Obtain a temporary certificate of registration and the 'Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal'.
required_dossiers: Executed incorporation document (private deed or public deed)
Formulario Único de Registro (pre-completed by the Chamber)
Pre-RUT registration (if obtained) or no-tax identification
Payment receipt of registration fees
Certificate of name availability (valid within 30 days)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a 'requerimiento' (request for correction), provide missing documentation within ten business days; if the request is dismissed, appeal before the 'Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio'.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with DIAN (RUT and Electronic Signature)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — Registro Único Tributario via 'Módulo de Registro' in official portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued 'Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal', register the S.A.S. in the RUT as a taxpayer, selecting the applicable tax treatment and ancillary obligations. Obtain the expedited RUT including electronic signature activation for e-invoicing and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate (original)
Legal representative's RUT or passport
Power-of-attorney or express authorization, if applicable
Bank reference for location
Completed RUT form (provided online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT is denied or query is raised, submit a correction via 'talento humano' or follow the 'Validación de datos' procedure before the DIAN office; constitute appeal within 5 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Corporate Books Registration and Bank Mandate Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (book inventory) and any commercial bank registered with Colombia's Financial Superintendence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company's share ledger and minutes book with the same Chamber within one month of incorporation (no registration fee for books if filings are done electronically). Open a corporate checking account with a local bank, providing the registration certificate and board resolution appointing the legal representative.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Notarized board resolution appointing officers
Registered corporate books (share ledger and minutes)
Taxpayer ID (RUT)
Original and copy of legal representative's ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank returns the application, adjust the beneficiation checklist (e.g., update corporate beneficial owners) and resubmit. For Chamber book registration, comply with physical formatting rules and re-file.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (INVIMA) — Dirección de Dispositivos Médicos y Otras Tecnologías
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Dispositivo Médico (Clase IIB/III) para Monitores de Signos Vitales, y Certificado de Buenas Prácticas de Manufactura (BPM) para Fabricación y Ensamble

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) o Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) según la ubicación de la planta
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría C (Licencia Ambiental Automática/Registro) — el ensamble de equipos electrónicos de bajo impacto requiere solo un registro de generadores de residuos peligrosos y una verificación ambiental previa. No se exige Estudio de Impacto Ambiental integral dado el volumen de producción (≤1 ton/día de componentes electrónicos). Para actividades con soldadura, se requiere permiso de emisión de gases.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Vertimientos de agua residual industrial conforme a Resolución 0631 de 2015 (pH 6-9, DBO5 ≤ 50 mg/L, SST ≤ 30 mg/L). Emisiones de COV de procesos de soldadura limitadas bajo la Resolución 0909 de 2008 y el Protocolo de Producción Más Limpia. Manejo de residuos peligrosos (baterías, plásticos, microchips) según Decreto 1076 de 2015, Resolución 1362 de 2007, con manifestación de generador ante la autoridad ambiental.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de inspección técnica del Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos (hidrantes, extintores, rutas de evacuación); visto bueno de cargas estructurales bajo NSR-10; y certificación del Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) según Resolución 0312 de 2019 (formulario de evaluación inicial, plan de emergencias, exámenes médicos ocupacionales).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - www.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity or an S.A.S. must obtain an NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) by filing an immediate electronic registration with DIAN through its 'Registro Único Tributario (RUT)' module. For a foreign legal entity without a Colombian branch, a local legal representative or tax attorney must be appointed, execute a power of attorney before a Colombian notary, and present the RUT application plus certified corporate documents (e.g., certificate of incorporation, bylaws) with legalization and official translation into Spanish. DIAN assigns the NIT upon identity validation and completion of the 'Pre-RUT' process; the RUT also records the VAT-responsible status (responsable del IVA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. An S.A.S. is per se a Colombian income-tax taxpayer and cannot elect pass-through treatment. No hybrid mismatch entity election is available under the Código Tributario, although certain investment vehicles or consortia (consorcios/unión temporal) may apply separate transparency rules under Articles 18 and 368 E.T.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for legal entities: every S.A.S. or foreign entity carrying out taxable activities or importing goods into Colombia must register as a VAT-responsible person in the RUT. Natural persons with income below 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 164,727,500 in 2024) may be non-responsible for VAT, but corporations are automatically responsible.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta - FE) is mandatory for all VAT-responsible entities. Each invoice must be transmitted in real time to DIAN's validation services using XML/factura electrónica format, include the CUDE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) and QR code, and be authorized by DIAN before dispatch. Export invoices must incorporate the exporter's RUT, the DEX number, and customs authorization. DIAN also requires 'validación previa' for all FE via web services with digital signature, generated through authorized software providers or DIAN's free app.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exenta de IVA, 0%) applies to definitive exports of tangible goods (e.g., patient monitors) when the goods physically leave Colombia. The taxpayer must hold a valid export license for the goods, register the export operation in DIAN's customs system (Export Declaration - DEX), and demonstrate the legal transfer of ownership to a foreign buyer. Complementary services (maintenance, calibration) qualify only if they are directly linked to the exported goods and performed for an overseas recipient under Article 481 E.T.; call center or software services must meet territorial-use requirements for zero-rated offshore services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación - DEX) submitted electronically through DIAN/VUCE
Bill of Lading (BL) or Airwaybill (AWB) evidencing physical departure of the monitors
Inward Remittance Certificate / Certificado de Compensación de Divisas (CCC) issued by an authorized Colombian financial intermediary
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Exporters are subject to mandatory documentary audit by DIAN and the customs authority. If zero-rating is claimed with false or inexact documentation, DIAN may deny the refund, assess an inflation penalty of up to 100% of the tax omitted (Article 648 E.T.), and impose a customs penalty equal to 30% of the value of the mis-declared merchandise (Law 1609/2016). Criminal tax fraud (Articles 434A/434B C.P.) and customs smuggling (Law 1762/2015) expose officers to imprisonment from 4 to 12 years and additional fines. Refunds are subject to retrospective clawback for up to five tax years where the supporting DEX, B/L, FX repatriation and export records are not upheld.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (BRC), with regulatory oversight jointly exercised by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) and the customs/tax authority, Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN). The foreign exchange system is governed by the political constitution, Ley 9 de 1991, Decreto 1735 de 1993, and the compendium of exchange regulations contained in Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83 of BRC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is fully convertible for current-account transactions, including registered trade and services payments. Capital-account inflows, including direct foreign investment, must be channelled through an authorised foreign exchange market intermediary (IMC) and registered with BRC via the Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional (Formulario No. 6) to guarantee lawful future dividend remittance, capital reduction, and repatriation. Non-registered investments lose the right to access the official FX market for profit outbound transfers. Trade dividends are otherwise subject to Colombian dividend withholding provisions under Law 2277 of 2022, without structural conversion restrictions. Practical hurdles include timely filing of the investment declaration, verifiable source of funds evidence, and consistent use of the IMC for all inward/outward clearing transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombian exporters of goods, including medical devices and electronic monitors, must channel export proceeds through an IMC. The BRC compendium (Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83) permits a maximum collection period of 13 months from the date of shipment or from the contractual due date, whichever is applicable, subject to the terms of the underlying export contract. There is no fixed percentage conversion mandate at the statutory level; the exporter must surrender or credit 100% of the export foreign currency to an IMC account, or to a compensation account (cuenta de compensación) authorised by BRC, within the applicable regulatory window (typically not exceeding 4 months of holding abroad). All collections must be evidenced by the declaración de cambio for goods exports filed with the IMC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.additional_fx_controls: All transactions exceeding the BRC de minimis threshold must be canalised through IMCs. Invoices, customs declarations, transport documents, and contract master agreements must be retained for 5 years to support the exchange declarations. Use of unofficial crypto corridors or offshore wallets as substitute settlement rails for trade flows is strictly prohibited. Foreign investor registration with BRC and DIAN corroboration is a precondition for outbound capital remittance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Inversión) and Operational Settlement Account
Operational Account, Payroll, and Corporate Treasury Ledger
Trade Finance Settlement Account and Working Capital Escrow
FX Derivative Collateral Account and Operational Current Account
Commercial Escrow and Trade Custody Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW for primary treasury rails. Colombian law reserves deposit-taking and current-account services to licensed credit institutions (banks, financial corporations, and savings corporations) regulated by the SFC. Foreign fintech companies and cross-border EMI services (for example, Wise, Payoneer, or Mercury) are not authorised to hold COP-based demand deposits or execute domestic ACH clearing without a local banking licence. Their lawful utility is restricted to auxiliary receivables/payables collection where the underlying FX transaction is extinguished through a licensed local IMC. EMI accounts must never receive Colombian export proceeds directly unless the funds are repatratriated and channelled through an IMC within the BRC timeline. The compliance risk of using unlicensed EMI settlement for import disbursements is material and may trigger DIAN customs valuation adjustments and SFC enforcement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding of a non-resident-owned S.A.S. is legally possible under SFC digital KYC standards, but Tier-1 Colombian banks commonly exercise discretion and require the appointed legal representative to appear in person or by videoconference for a structured KYC interview. Where 100% of directors and shareholders are foreign, the bank will typically demand: (i) apostilled corporate documents from the jurisdiction of incorporation; (ii) notarised power of attorney granted to a Colombian legal representative or a designated treasury officer; (iii) certified translation of the constitutive documents; (iv) evidence of a physical operating premise in Colombia, demonstrated by a lease agreement and utility bills; and (v) a board resolution designating the account signatories and confirming the intended use of accounts. Physical presence of the principal is strongly recommended during initial onboarding to reduce bank risk appetite and accelerate the opening timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wholly foreign-owned S.A.S. with no Colombian employees, no local payroll, and no visible operational footprint during onboarding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of existence and legal representation issued by the Cámara de Comercio (must be less than 90 days old); apostilled incorporation charter and board resolutions; executed commercial lease agreement for the Colombian assembly/calibration site; Colombian employment contracts or staffing agreement with a local HR provider; INVIMA sanitary registration or import licence for the ECG monitor; ISO 13485 (medical device QMS) certificate; description of manufacturing workflow and floor plan supporting physical operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection materially exceeding the registered equity or inconsistent shareholder wealth profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call minutes and shareholder approval records; pro-forma financial statements of the foreign parent; six to twelve months of bank statements for the remitting entity/source of funds account; source-of-wealth memorandum (asset distribution, revenue streams, sale of business, or financing agreement); affidavits from the beneficial owners; the bank reference letter of the remitting institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential use of non-banking corridors, offshore payments, or crypto-facing intermediaries for trade settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed international sale contracts (in English/Spanish); purchase orders and pro-forma invoices from verified suppliers; logistics and bill-of-lading documentation; DIAN export/import customs declarations; declaration that all payments will clear exclusively via an IMC; no involvement of unlicensed payment providers in cross-border settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO registry inconsistency or opacity in the ultimate shareholder chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Org chart tracing beneficial ownership through each intermediary holding company; apostilled share register or UBO registry extract; notarised declarations signed by each cascading beneficial owner; SFC-compliant SARLAFT beneficiary questionnaire; sanctions and PEP screening reports for each UBO; explanation for any change in control within the preceding 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical device end-user destination high-risk jurisdiction or suspected restricted technology transfer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export licence evidence (INVIMA and DIAN permits); end-user certificate and denial/restricted-party screening results for clients; detailed technical specification sheet consistent with ISIC 3250 patient-monitoring products; CTH (Harmonized System) classification and declaration of conformity (CE/FDA certifications as applicable); independent annual audit report if export volumes are substantial.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholder transfers USD/EUR from an overseas bank to the beneficiary account of CO_SAS held at a Colombian Tier-1 bank via SWIFT MT103. The wire instruction must clearly indicate 'Aporte de capital - Inversión directa de capital en CO_SAS' and reference the NIT (Colombian tax ID) of the S.A.S. The beneficiary bank, acting as an IMC, credits the funds to the capital escrow account and converts foreign currency into COP at the prevailing market rate. The IMC files the Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional (Formulario No. 6) with BRC; the investor must maintain a file copy of the wire, the IMC receipt, the capital registration certificate, and the stamped exchange declaration, as these will govern future dividend remittance, capital reduction, and liquidation proceeds. For submission, a certified translation of the board resolution approving the capital call and a police-checked source-of-funds memo are required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements follow three authorised clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account component purchases and supplier payments, accompanied by a clear trade purpose code and reference to the underlying purchase order; (ii) MT700/MT707 irrevocable documentary letters of credit for high-value calibration modules and raw-material imports, with performance/guarantee instruments structured as MT760 standby letters of credit for advance payments; and (iii) SWIFT member-to-member transfer for intra-group cross-border services, with the corresponding tax withholding certificates and service agreements. All import-related payments must be channelled via an IMC and reconciled with DIAN customs declarations; the importer must file the relevant export/import exchange declaration with the IMC before or at the time of disbursement. Payment matching is mandatory: the amount, currency, and timing must align with the customs valuation (Declaración Andina de Valor) and supporting invoices to avoid penalties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable COP/USD forward contracts (forwards de tasa de cambio) traded with authorised IMCs under BRC hedging provisions and backed by real trade exposure
Non-deliverable COP/USD forwards (NDFs) settled in COP with local counterparties under ISDA documentation for hedge-efficient treasury structures
FX swaps (simultaneous spot and forward legs) executed with local banks to cover short-term liquidity mismatches in COP
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term matching of USD import liabilities and COP-denominated working capital assets
Limited FX options (call/put structures) permitted where the underlying exposure is verified by the IMC and confirmed to serve a hedging, not speculative, purpose
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.settlement_contingency_and_liquidity_buf: Maintain a minimum COP liquidity buffer of three months of operating expenditure in a current account at the IMC. Hold a contingency USD line in a foreign currency deposit account at the same Tier-1 bank to cover import urgency without triggering premature conversion. All currency movements require simultaneous exchange declaration so that the S.A.S. remains continuously compliant with BRC channelisation rules and audit-ready for DIAN and SFC examinations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No universal tax holiday for a standard S.A.S.; available preferential deductions include a 100% additional deduction for qualifying investments in research, science, technology and innovation, and a reduced 20% CIT rate for entities legally operating within Free Trade Zones.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios), filed electronically through DIAN MUISCA (www.dian.gov.co).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due in the following fiscal year according to the DIAN calendar based on the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT, generally between early September and late October of the year following the taxable year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: NIT, legal name, fiscal year, CIIU economic activity code, tax classification and main address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian S.A.S. files under its own NIT; foreign shareholders are not identified on this field unless the entity is transparent or the shareholder acts through a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income (ingresos brutos): includes all revenue from assembly, calibration, sale and technical service of electronic patient monitoring ECG equipment, plus any incidental income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Colombian-source revenue is reportable; foreign branch or export revenues are included only if attributable to a Colombian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses: direct material, import costs, calibration labor, depreciation, maintenance and financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to related suppliers must satisfy Colombian transfer-pricing documentation standards to remain deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss (renta líquida): gross income less allowable deductions, costs and recoverable provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders' administrative or financing overheads may be deductible only under arm's-length and treaty provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable and exempt income: legal exemptions such as treaty-exempt profits or tax-incentive income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt income must be supported by applicable DTA provisions and beneficial-ownership evidence; otherwise it remains taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (renta líquida gravable): net income less non-taxable income and tax-loss carry-forwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NOL carry-forwards are allowed for up to 12 years; the loss year and available compensation must be proved to DIAN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable: taxable income multiplied by 35%, reduced by tax credits, advances, withholding credits and incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax on dividends distributed to foreign shareholders is a separate obligation; any non-resident tax credit is permitted only under a DTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of tax due per month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax; where no tax is due, 0.5% of gross income per month (cap 5% of gross income, minimum 10 UVT). An inaccurate return triggers an understatement penalty of up to 20% (Art. 648 ET), plus monthly mora interest. Persistent non-compliance may lead to RUT suspension and collection proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 7.5% withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders from already-taxed profits; 35% for dividends derived from non-taxable/exempt profits; a 3% surcharge applies from FY2023 when the shareholder is resident in a non-cooperative or low-tax jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (1) obtain the foreign tax authority's Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) for the shareholder; (2) deliver the TRC and a Beneficial-Owner Declaration (declaración de beneficiario efectivo) to the Colombian payer before distribution; (3) retain records for a mandatory period; (4) where excess has been withheld, submit the electronic DIAN refund/reimbursement application with the full dossier. The payer may apply the treaty rate at source only when the documentation is complete and demonstrates absence of conduit arrangements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding rate on gross IP payments is 15%; DTA rates commonly range from 0% to 10% depending on the jurisdiction. Interest: statutory withholding rate is 15% on gross debt interest; treaty rates are typically 5%–10%, and sometimes 0% for government or export-backed financing, always conditioned on treaty residence, beneficial ownership and substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when the Colombian taxpayer's gross income or gross assets exceed 135,000 UVT (approx. COP 6.35 billion for FY2024) or when related-party transactions exceed 62,200 UVT (approx. COP 2.93 billion). Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated gross revenue exceeds 180,000 UVT (approx. COP 8.47 billion for FY2024).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not enforce a standalone ESR (Economic Substance Regulations) framework comparable to the UAE; however, the general anti-abuse rule (Art. 869 ET), the substance-over-form doctrine and DTA beneficial-ownership requirements impose a real economic-substance threshold. The Colombian S.A.S. must maintain genuine operational presence, calibrated manufacturing capacity, decision-making power and documented technical staff to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fraudulently omitting revenues from ECG monitor calibration services, overstating cross-border component costs, using fictitious invoices, or destroying books to reduce the taxable base in Form 110.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code Art. 405A: imprisonment from 3 to 6 years and a fine equal to 100%–300% of the evaded tax. DIAN additionally imposes a 20% understatement penalty, mora interest, cancellation of tax registration and seizure of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or legal representatives who sign fraudulent returns are criminally liable; preventive travel bans, asset embargoes and temporary suspension of the company's permit to operate are possible. Civil liability extends to restituting the evaded tax and damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Shell Company / Sociedad de Fachada
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating the S.A.S. with nominal or fake domicile, no operational substance, and using it solely to route dividends, royalties, or technical-service fees to a foreign related party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the entity under Art. 869 ET and tax the beneficial owner directly; penalties include 20% fraud surcharge and mora interest. Under commercial law, the company may be subject to cancellation of registration and forfeiture of improperly distributed profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Colombian courts apply veil-piercing to impose joint and several liability on directors and nominee shareholders. Criminal fraud laws may lead to imprisonment for up to 12 years if public funds are involved; travel bans and asset freezing are common enforcement measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the TP informative return or Local/Master File, omitting related-party transactions, or filing with manipulated intra-group margins for calibration services and royalty payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 1212 ET imposes a fine of 10% of the total value of related-party transactions not properly documented; DIAN may recharacterize the transactions, assess additional taxable income at 35%, and apply mora interest plus a 20% fraud penalty for intentional misstatements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign falsely documented TP returns face criminal liability for falsifying private records, punishable by up to 8 years' imprisonment; civil liability covers the additional tax and fines, and courts may issue travel bans and prevent the director from serving in any Colombian company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the S.A.S. to receive or disburse proceeds from corrupt public-hospital procurement tenders, kickback schemes linked to ECG equipment sales, or concealment of cash payments without the mandatory SAGRILAFT controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code Art. 323: imprisonment from 10 to 20 years (aggravated to 30 years under certain circumstances) and fines from 250 to 15,000 SMLMV. The company may be dissolved, its assets subjected to extinción de dominio, and its registration cancelled.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and directors who omit AML controls may be indicted as co-authors; personal assets can be frozen, travel bans imposed, and convictions lead to disqualification from public tenders for up to 20 years and a permanent board-ban.
